beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:painting the picture, hushed]Off the Bahamas, half a mile of flat, ^squared stones lies on the sea floor. [act:wonder, slowly][tune:rise]A ^road, under the ^sea?
[d:tension][act:intrigued, the coincidence][tune:fall]It was found in the ^very year a famous psychic said Atlantis would ^rise again.

[d:calm][act:storytelling, even]In {1940|nineteen forty}, the American psychic Edgar Cayce said part of Atlantis would reappear near ^Bimini, a tiny island in the Bahamas. [act:quoting him, lightly][tune:fall]^Expect it in {'68|sixty-eight}, he said. [go:1|0][act:the payoff, measured][tune:fall]In {1968|nineteen sixty-eight}, divers ^found the blocks. [act:a quiet detail][tune:fall]Five and a half metres ^down, in clear, shallow water.

[d:build][act:giving their case fairly][tune:fall]Too neat to be ^natural, say the believers. [act:laying out the evidence, open]^Straight lines, ^square corners, and some blocks seem to sit on smaller stones, like ^props, the way a builder levels a ^slab.
[d:build][act:conceding, fair][tune:fall]And they have a real point: the Bahama banks ^really were dry land in the Ice Age, when the sea stood far ^lower.

[d:build][act:turning the page, brisk][tune:fall]Now the ^rock. [act:explaining, clear and friendly]It's ^beachrock: beach sand, glued into stone by lime, right where the tide comes and ^goes. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Seawater soaks the sand, dries, and leaves its lime behind, like the white crust inside a ^kettle. [act:the key point, a little delight][tune:fall]It forms ^fast here, and it cracks into squares all by ^itself, like mud drying in a ^puddle.

[d:build][go:3|0][sfx:shimmer][act:the evidence, crisp][tune:fall]Geologists drilled ^seventeen cores, little tubes of rock, from neighbouring ^blocks. [act:clear, visual, unhurried][tune:fall]Inside, the layers run on from block to block, at the same tilt, like ^one slab broken in ^place. [p:0.93][act:explaining, simple][tune:fall]Blocks cut and laid by builders would tilt every which ^way.

[d:reveal][act:leaning in, the clincher][tune:fall]And the ^dates. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]Radiocarbon dating reads the age of shells: their carbon fades at a steady pace, like a candle burning ^down. [act:precise, steady][tune:level]The shells in the stone are about ^three and a half ^thousand years old. [act:quick, pointed][tune:fall]The cement that glues them, ^younger. [sfx:hit][act:the sting, quiet and firm][tune:fall]So the stone didn't even ^exist when the Ice Age ended.
[d:aside][act:warm, a twinkle][tune:fall]The sea is a very good ^bricklayer.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]An Ice Age ^road? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Ruled out*, by the rock's ^own age. [act:fair, opening a door][tune:rise]People ^reusing the slabs ^later, as a quay or a pavement? [act:honest, even][tune:fallrise]^Not ruled out. [act:plain, gently closing it][tune:fall]But ^nothing points to it yet.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, affectionate][tune:fall]A beautiful ^coincidence, laid by the ^sea.
